main_text.l: tradit, ut utrique humani erroris & infirmitatis sensu admoniti, Deo gloriam dent, & iterum in Domino coalescant. Tales fuerunt συμφωνίας Pauli & Barnabæ: Act. 15.39. Augustini & Hieronymi super dicto Pauli, Gal. 2. Ioannis Chrysostomi & Epiphanii, propter Anthropomorphiticam hæresin: quam ille quidem pie refutabat, hic autem, in gratiam Theophili Alexandrini, parum prudenter tuebatur. Etsi autem hi duo eruperunt in voces manticas, cum ille quidem huic diceret, Non redibis ad tuos vivos: hic autem illi responderet, Nec tu morieris Episcopus: ac utrique dicto euentus respondit: tamen οἱ τοιοῦτοι ἡ θεη-γορεῖ ἡ θεοφιλὲς ἀνθρωποι, in gratiam repositi sunt. Ac videtur μεταμέλεια Epiphanio soluenti Constantinopoli dictasse hanc vocem: Σπάσθω ἐγώ. Ἀφήμι δὲ ὑμῖν τὰ βασιλέα ἡ τῶν πόλιν ἡ τῶν ὑπόκεισιν. quam eandem sententiam nostro tempore multi præstantes Christi serui & Ecclesiarum pastores, pulsi e suis sedibus, pronunciare possent.
5. Nonnunquam malos in bonorum manus tradit: ut Saulem Regem bis tradidit Deus in manus Dauidis, qui etiam ab uncto

page.notes: Greek passages transcribed from a small, worn, partly unclear print; the Greek readings in the 2nd and 3rd Greek phrases are doubtful and should be checked against the scan. The line "Nec tu morieris Episcope" and the Latin "vivos" (for "tuos vi-uus") are doubtful; "Episcopus" read as printed. The word "quam" line and "Epiphanio" are read as printed. The bottom word "uncto" is a line-end fragment and continues on the next page. Possible sign of an omitted accent in some Greek words.
